Compared against the same weekday, not an all-days average, because weekends here run roughly a third below weekdays. Anything inside 10% either way is ordinary week-to-week movement. Today is the red bar and is still counting.

This will not match the number in Google Analytics, and that is deliberate. Analytics reported 9,262 organic visits that day against the 4,390 here. Same Analytics property, narrower cut: US visitors on www.testing.com, counted as engaged visits. Engaged is the important part. Analytics does not filter crawlers, and they are most of our raw visits, but a crawler loads a page and leaves so it never counts as engaged. Using the raw number would show traffic lurching around when only bot volume moved. Analytics also revises the last day or two upward as it finishes processing, so this figure can rise slightly.
impact_html:
Did our changes work?

One verdict per change, each measured on the number it should actually move
STD pricing page rebuiltfunnelAug 26 · 9:57 AM

Our main STD pricing page was rebuilt to Allen's new design, mobile first, with the trust rail carrying the Trustpilot rating and CLIA badge, new copy throughout, and every CTA going straight to the cart.

Cannot measuremeasured on /std-test-pricing/

Cart tracking on the site stopped on Aug 27, and every one of the 6 full days since this shipped is affected. Stripe kept taking orders throughout, so this is a measurement outage and not a drop in sales. Use the checkout chart below in the meantime, and come back here once tracking is fixed.

Place My Order double-click fixfunnelAug 21 · 8:30 AM

The button stayed live after the first click, so a second click created another Stripe invoice for the same order. Five of the first 19 paid orders went through two or three invoices.

Monetization livelaunchAug 18 · 12:00 AM

Checkout opened on testing.com. First customer order came through at 1:03 AM from Google organic.

This is the starting line, so there is nothing before it to compare against.

Cart rate since launch

Carts per 1,000 organic visits, split by the section each change affected, with the whole site dashed for reference. Only changes measured on cart rate appear here. Checkout changes move a different number and are judged on their own cards above, and a change to a page people click through to rather than land on gets its own chart below. A section line is the only place a section-level change can show up: STD GEO is about a tenth of our visits, so a big move there barely dents the sitewide line. Carts are the measure rather than orders because orders run single digits a day and cannot separate signal from noise for weeks. 16 days of data so far.

Cart rate on /std-test-pricing/

Share of organic visits to /std-test-pricing/ that add something to the cart. Counted on the page people viewed, not the page they landed on, which is why this is a separate chart and not another line above. Almost nobody arrives on the pricing page from search, they click through to it, so its landing-page numbers run single digits a day while it fires more than half of every cart on the site. One visit counts once here however many tests it adds, so this is a share of people rather than a count of clicks. The two charts count different groups of people and their heights do not compare.

Reached checkout, the measure that kept working

Organic visits that got as far as a checkout page, per 1,000 organic visits. This one comes from page views rather than from the site's own cart code, so it is the only funnel line still recording while cart tracking is down, and it is drawn unshaded for that reason. Nobody reaches checkout without carting first, so read it as a stand-in for the two charts above. Do not read it against them: reaching checkout is a later step than adding to the cart, so this number is lower by construction and the heights do not compare. The shape is the part that carries over.

Changes are recorded by hand, big ones only, and each needs the right scope and metric. To add one, edit changes.json.

attribution_html:
Where orders come from

Google Analytics, today so far · treat as directional, not exact
Bot traffic has been removed from every number in this section. Datacenter crawlers from Google Cloud and AWS hit this site hard, loading a page for two seconds and leaving. On 2026-09-02 that was 4,819 of 8,259 US sessions. Visit counts below are engaged sessions, meaning a real person read the page. Google Analytics' own dashboard does not filter this, so its traffic numbers will look several times larger than these and its conversion rates several times worse.
Read this before quoting anything below. The cart columns below are empty because the site is not recording cart events today, not because nobody carted. These figures come from Google Analytics and are much less reliable than the revenue above. Analytics data runs through 1:52 PM PT, about 2h 4m behind this page. Analytics is also not recording checkout correctly yet: it logged 0 payment steps today against 12 real paid orders, and our purchase event sends no order value, so Analytics reports $0 revenue no matter what sells. Use it to see which pages bring people in, never to count orders or money.

notice_html: The site stopped recording its checkout events part way through Aug 27, so every cart and checkout figure below is wrong from that day on. Since Aug 28 purchase, email capture and payment events have logged nothing at all, and cart counts collapsed with them, while Stripe went on taking orders: 55 paid orders landed across those days. Aug 27 itself is drawn, but it is an undercount rather than a fall. Orders, revenue and traffic come from Stripe and from page views, so those are unaffected and can be read normally. For the funnel, use the checkout chart in "Did our changes work?", which is measured a different way and kept recording throughout. Days with no tracking are drawn as gaps, never as zeros.
